paper_citation: Farah, E.N. et al. Spatially organized cellular communities form the developing human heart. Nature 627, 854–864 (2024).
notes: Gold claims are scorer-only. Agents must never see this file.

claims.statement: Developing human heart tissue organizes into spatially restricted cellular communities with enriched co-localization of specific cell-type pairs rather than random mixing.
claims.evidence_locus: main text / abstract — spatially organized cellular communities

claims.statement: Adventitial-like fibroblasts (adFibro) and lymphatic endothelial cells (LEC) form reciprocal spatial interfaces constituting a fibro–lymphatic niche with distinct chemokine / trafficking programs.
claims.evidence_locus: spatial community analyses involving fibroblast–lymphatic interfaces

claims.statement: Specialized non-chamber cardiomyocyte populations (e.g. AVC-like / IFT-like) occupy boundary or conduction-associated niches with enriched fibroblast or neuronal neighbors and distinct matrix or ion-handling programs.
